item.research_question: How can bulk soft magnetic materials achieve a combination of high strength and good ductility without significantly deteriorating their soft magnetic properties (specifically coercivity)?
item.material_system: Non-equiatomic Fe35-x/3Co30-x/3Ni30-x/3Ta5Alx (x = 3, 5, 7 at%) high-entropy alloys, specifically the 7Al-HEA variant with a face-centered cubic matrix and L12 nanoprecipitates.
item.processing_route: As-cast plates (10-mm thick) were hot-rolled at 1473 K to 50% thickness reduction, followed by 10-min homogenization at 1473 K and water quenching.
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature; magnetic properties measured via vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) and magneto-optical Kerr microscopy; microstructure analyzed via TEM, APT, and 4D-STEM.
key_findings: The 7Al-HEA achieved an ultimate tensile strength of 1526 MPa with a tensile elongation of 15.3%.
The yield strength of the 7Al-HEA (1202 MPa) was approximately 245% higher than the base alloy (501 MPa).
The coercivity of the 7Al-HEA was 10.7 Oe, only marginally increased from 8.6 Oe in the 3Al-HEA.
The saturation magnetization (Ms) of the 7Al-HEA was 88 Am2 kg-1, compared to 105 Am2 kg-1 for the 3Al-HEA.
The L12 nanoprecipitates had an average size of 13.5 ± 2.5 nm and a volume fraction greater than 42% in the 7Al-HEA.
Dynamic microband refinement reduced the mean distance between parallel microbands from 735 ± 251 nm to 163 ± 35 nm as local strain increased from 30% to 50%.
The 7Al-HEA maintained 61% of its room temperature Ms value at 773 K.
The lattice strain at the coherent interface varied between -0.2% and 0.5% for the 7Al-HEA.
item.mechanism: Strength is enhanced by massive solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening via shearing of coherent ordered L12 nanoprecipitates, and dynamic microband refinement. Soft magnetic properties are preserved because the full coherency between the nanoprecipitates and the matrix creates negligible distortion fields, resulting in insignificant pinning of Bloch domain walls compared to grain boundaries.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that conventional strengthening approaches usually significantly deteriorate soft magnetic properties due to Bloch wall interactions with defects.
item.future_work: The findings provide guidance for developing new high-performance materials with an excellent combination of mechanical and soft magnetic properties as needed for the electrification of transport and industry.
quotes: Compared to the alloy in precipitate‐free state, the alloy variant with a large volume fraction (>42%) of nanoprecipitates achieves significantly enhanced strength (≈1526 MPa) at good ductility (≈15%), while the coercivity is only marginally increased (<10.7 Oe).

The ordered nanoprecipitates and the resulting dynamic microband refinement in the matrix significantly strengthen the HEAs, while full coherency between the nanoprecipitates and the matrix leads at the same time to the desired insignificant pinning of the magnetic domain walls.

The high lattice coherency between the homogeneously dispersed nanoprecipitates and the alloy matrix creates only negligible distortion fields on magnetic domain wall motion and contributes significantly to the strength of the material.
